children: Oil rose Monday as a resurgence in Middle East hostilities boosted concerns over supply disruptions in the region.

U.S. forces attacked two Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, the U.S. Central Command said, marking the first American strike in weeks. U.S. Central Command said that the Iranian launchers, which were deployed on Larak Island, were preparing to fire rockets filled with sea mines into the strait when they were struck.

Shortly after the U.S. strike, American forces defended against missiles launched at Jordan, according to U.S. military officials. Jordan hosts almost 4,000 U.S. troops and is an important staging ground for U.S. military operations throughout the Middle East.

"The path to a deal to reopen the Strait [of Hormuz] remains elusive," ANZ Research analysts said in a note. "President Trump signaled he won't lift a naval blockade on Iranian ports, a key demand from the Islamic Republic. He's also not interested in returning to the terms of the June ceasefire," the ANZ analysts added.

The Trump administration has said that it is focusing on ramped-up economic sanctions and its maritime blockade to attempt to compel Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz and make concessions on its nuclear program.
Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures rose 1.1% to $84.32 per barrel and front-month Brent crude oil futures added 1.3% to $89.24 a barrel, ICE data showed.

Equity markets across the Asia-Pacific region broadly declined after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole economic policy symposium last Friday lifted prospects for interest-rate increases by the U.S. central bank.
"The main theme was the hawkish repricing of Fed expectations following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a note.

Warsh said he saw little sign that borrowing and lending conditions were restraining the U.S. economy, and that better inflation readings this summer hadn't convinced him the underlying trend was improving.
"We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do," Warsh said.
"The comments were more explicit than markets had anticipated and reinforced the view that the Fed remains prepared to resume tightening," the Commerzbank analysts added.
Japan's Nikkei Stock Average fell 1.7%, South Korea's Kospi dropped 1.9% and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 benchmark index edged 0.1% lower.
U.S. stock-index futures also declined. The eMini Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 0.5%, the eMini S&P 500 futures fell 0.3% and the eMini Dow futures were 0.2% lower.
